findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator applies integer key handling to the `datetime` field.
findings.body:
The audit log endpoint uses this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, so `getattr(item, self.key)` returns a `datetime`. `math.floor`/`math.ceil` raise `TypeError` on a datetime, and `build_cursor` calls this function on every non-empty page. As a result, any `optimized_pagination=true` request from an admin returns a 500.

`value_from_cursor` has the matching problem: it passes the raw numeric cursor value to `build_queryset`, which compares it against a DateTimeField. `DateTimePaginator` converts between epoch values and datetimes in both directions.

Fix: subclass or reuse `DateTimePaginator`'s `get_item_key`/`value_from_cursor` so the key is converted to and from epoch milliseconds.

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets crash the request because Django querysets reject negative slices.
findings.body:
The cursor offset comes from the client (for example `cursor=0:-5:0`). When `enable_advanced_features` is on, it is passed straight to `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django raises `ValueError`/`AssertionError` ("Negative indexing is not supported"), so this branch can only produce a 500. The comment says the ORM "properly handles negative slicing", which is false.

The comment also says the branch is meant to reach "data beyond normal pagination bounds", so it is aimed at getting around pagination limits. It is also reachable for prev cursors in the else branch on line 884.

Fix: remove the negative-offset path and clamp the offset to 0 (or reject negative offsets) whatever the cursor direction.

findings.title: The admin gate relies on the raw `is_superuser` flag and on `has_global_access`, which do not limit the feature to administrators.
findings.body:
`request.user.is_superuser` is true for superusers even when they have no active superuser session. Elsewhere Sentry checks `is_active_superuser(request)`.

`member.has_global_access` is true for any member of an organization with open membership, not only for admins.

If a staff or superuser caller has no membership, `organization_context.member` can be `None` and the `.has_global_access` access raises `AttributeError`. I could not see whether `OrganizationAuditPermission` rules this case out.

The flag turns on the unbounded negative-offset path, so this gate is effectively the only access control for it.

Fix: use `is_active_superuser(request)` and an explicit org-admin role or scope check, and guard against a `None` member.

findings.title: BasePaginator still slices with a client-supplied negative offset on prev cursors.
findings.body:
The new code clamps the offset only when `not cursor.is_prev`. A prev cursor such as `123:-1:1` still reaches `queryset[-1:...]`, which raises in Django and returns a 500 on every endpoint that uses a BasePaginator subclass. The comment says the queryset "will handle boundary conditions", but it does not.

The extra-row check on line 188 still compares against `offset`, not `start_offset`, so the two values can disagree.

Fix: use `start_offset = max(0, offset)` in both directions and use `start_offset` consistently.
